hn-50224463.t: No signs of AI payoff outside the tech sector
hn-50224463.s: Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech. Subscribe for daily updates.
ex: Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech. Revenue per worker is rising for the Mag 7 but is flat for the S&P 493, see the first chart below. Profit margins are rising for the Mag 7 but are flat for the S&P 493, see the second chart below. And there are still no signs of AI boosting productivity growth, see the third chart below. With no impact on the bottom line, mainstream corporate America is pulling back and starting to view token spending not as a source of growth but as a cost center that weighs on margins. VC-backed companies are spending more and more on tokens, but mainstream corporate America does not need the latest model and is unwilling to pay for it. As long as agentic AI and token spending are confined to a small part of the economy, the macroeconomic effects of AI will be very limited, see the fourth and fifth charts below.

hn-50224100.s: A memory-safe systems language with no heap allocator, garbage collector, or lifetime annotations. In this repository's benchmarks, Goose runs faster than C++ and Rust while using less memory.
ex: A memory-safe systems language with no heap allocator, garbage collector, or lifetime annotations. In this repository's benchmarks, Goose runs faster than C++ and Rust while using less memory. Tutorial · Reference · Specification · Packages · Samples · Benchmarks · Standard library Goose has syntax familiar to C and Rust programmers, but there is no heap. Every dynamic value lives inline on a data stack managed by the compiler. Growth advances a pointer, and memory is freed when its scope ends. The language's type and lifetime rules make this memory model safe to use. The tutorial walks through all of this by example, the reference covers the whole language topic by topic, the specification has the exact rules, and the benchmarks have the numbers, losses included. This section focuses on what distinguishes Goose. The tutorial explains these features in more detail, and the samples show them in thirty-one complete programs.

hn-50221676.t: Google illegally cut down 250K trees in Finland for data center
hn-50221676.s: The tech super giant – continuing its expansion of the booming artificial intelligence industry – cleared 816 acres of woodlands in Northern Finland, the Guardian reported Thursday.
ex: Google illegally demolished an estimated 250,000 trees in Finland to make way for a data center, leaving behind a lifeless mud wasteland that forced packs of wolves into a nearby town in search of food and infuriated locals, according to a report. The tech super giant – continuing its expansion of the booming artificial intelligence industry – cleared 816 acres of woodlands in Northern Finland, The Guardian reported Thursday. Google is accused of removing the trees and clearing the land before it had full approval — as Finnish law requires companies to complete a mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment before large-scale operations. Finnish officials, outraged by the mass destruction, suspended all development at two of Google’s data center sites to assess the environmental impact.

hn-50219177.t: Node2Shell evolves to HTTP2Shell, blast radius affects many HTTP libs and apps
hn-50219177.s: The Brotli flaw behind Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497) affects many libraries and applications using HTTP with Brotli or brotlicffi installed. Check your versions and upgrade to the fix.
ex: Brotli is a lossless compression algorithm and data format developed by Google. It’s a way to make data smaller for storage or sending over the internet. Software then unpacks it to recover the original data. It’s widely used for HTTP compression to compress web content such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder affecting versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms. This is the same Brotli decoder flaw behind Node2Shell announced a couple days ago. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted Brotli-compressed stream to corrupt memory, leak sensitive data, crash the process, or potentially execute arbitrary code. It carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2 (Critical), and Node.js is affected through its bundled Brotli library. A bug makes the Brotli decoder keep accepting more bytes when it should reject the data. Those bytes can overflow a small working buffer and damage the program’s memory.

hn-50220913.t: Elon Musk Just Gave Europe a Reason to Replace American Technology
hn-50220913.s: I’ve been in London for the last month and have heard policymakers react to the wake up call Elon Musk just delivered.
ex: I’ve been in London for the last month and have heard policymakers react to the wake up call Elon Musk just delivered. The decision of the U.S. to shut off intelligence and throttle the military version of Starlink called Starshield to Ukraine may have been a blip in the news in the US, but it has sent tremors across Europe. For years doomsayers in the UK and Europe were worried about the U.S. having a kill switch in weapon systems and critical commercial technology that could disconnect them at will. Most people, including me, thought that it was a paranoid fantasy. Until it happened. Seemingly on a whim of a single individual, (according to the Wall Street Journal) Elon Musk personally ordered the restrictions, and the effect was to tilt Russia’s war against Ukraine in favor of the Russians. This wasn’t an articulated U.S. foreign policy nor was it an announced act of the U.S. government.

hn-50217500.s: In September 2014 I published a short post announcing rqlite. The idea was simple: take SQLite, put a Raft log in front of it, and replicate every write to a cluster so that the loss of a node did…
ex: In September 2014 I published a short post announcing rqlite. The idea was simple: take SQLite, put a Raft log in front of it, and replicate every write to a cluster so that the loss of a node did not mean the loss of the data. The source went on GitHub that same weekend. As far as I can tell, that was the first open-source system to combine Raft and SQLite. Nobody else was doing it, and for several years nobody else tried. Today “distributed SQLite” is a category with a dozen projects in it, a few of them venture-funded, two of them acquired. Since the people now writing about the category tend to start the story around 2021, I thought I should write down the version that starts in 2014. I was there for all of it. The need was concrete. A clustered system I worked on at jut.io needed a small amount of relational storage, and the question of which node should hold it had no good answer. Replicating SQLite with a consensus protocol solved it.

hn-50218277.t: Indian government sites are serving revoked eMudhra certificates
hn-50218277.s: On 17th October, eight eMudhra intermediate CAs chaining to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 were found to have trivially recoverable private keys.
ex: On 17th October, eight eMudhra intermediate CAs chaining to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 were found to have trivially recoverable private keys. They were revoked the next day, and Mozilla and Chrome are now distrusting the G3 root. Separately, on 19th October eMudhra revoked 9,356 certificates on its unaffected RSA hierarchy (emSign Root CA - G1) with the reason “Superseded”. That batch matches every unexpired certificate missing a certificate-type policy OID required by emSign’s own CP/CPS (Bug 2082782). A security incident concerning eMudhra’s Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) was reported in the public domain. […] However, some social media accounts are indulging in fear mongering about the impact of this incident. […] The impact of this incident on Indian websites and applications have been very limited and for a very short interval. That last claim is wrong on both counts.
